who: Thomas Young; Jean-François Champollion; later scholars
corpus_at_decipherment: Thousands of facsimile inscriptions; Rosetta decree; Philae royal names; no exact contemporary count
method_steps: Cartouches and royal names → cross-script sound values → Coptic words/grammar → earlier Egyptian names → new inscriptions
notes: 1822 announcement; 1824 system; no instantaneous complete translation.
selected_stage: 1822 phonetic announcement
used_later_in_recovery: Champollion’s 1824 grammatical extension and earlier royal names.

who: Åkerblad; de Sacy; Young; Champollion; Brugsch and successors
corpus_at_decipherment: Rosetta Demotic/Greek text and documentary papyri; exact early corpus count unknown
method_steps: Proper names → parallel Greek clauses → links with hieratic/hieroglyphic forms → Coptic vocabulary → grammatical extension
notes: Timeline marks Åkerblad 1802, an initial phonetic advance; Brugsch and successors extended grammatical understanding through 1848/1855 and later.
selected_stage: 1802 Åkerblad name-letter stage
used_later_in_recovery: Young, Champollion and Brugsch extended phonetic and grammatical readings after 1802.

who: Grotefend; Rask; Burnouf; Lassen; Rawlinson; Hincks
corpus_at_decipherment: Short royal inscriptions at Persepolis and Hamadan; later long Behistun trilingual; count unknown
method_steps: Repeated royal formulae → dynastic names from Greek histories → Iranian/Indo-European comparison → expanded copies and grammar
notes: 1802 stage: de Sacy’s royal formula and Herodotus supplied external anchors. Parallel=no is contested: Daniels calls this a virtual bilingual. Iranian comparison available in outline; later refinements are separately labelled.
selected_stage: 1802 Grotefend royal-name stage
used_later_in_recovery: Rask, Burnouf and Lassen developed the Iranian comparisons after 1802; Rawlinson extended readings using Behistun.

who: Edward Hincks; Henry Rawlinson; Jules Oppert; William Henry Fox Talbot
corpus_at_decipherment: Royal texts; trilingual inscriptions; bricks and tablets; sign lists; exact contemporary count unknown
method_steps: Names across trilinguals → syllabic values, homophony and polyphony → Semitic grammar → independent sealed translations
notes: 1857 RAS test included Talbot; Babylonian and Assyrian are Akkadian varieties. Behistun was not the sole initial key.
selected_stage: 1857 RAS independent-translation stage

who: Hincks; Rawlinson; Oppert; Haupt; many later Sumerologists
corpus_at_decipherment: Akkadian–Sumerian lexical lists and bilinguals; later thousands of Tello documents; early count unknown
method_steps: Bilingual lexical lists → comparison of logographic and syllabic spellings → grammar → monolingual texts
notes: Timeline marks Haupt’s published Die sumerischen Familiengesetze (1879); the dissertation stage is 1878. This is language recovery within shared cuneiform, not an independent invention of a new script.
selected_stage: 1879 Haupt bilingual-publication stage

year_label: 1853 recovery stage; memoir in JRAS volume dated 1855
who: Nils Westergaard; Edward Hincks; Edwin Norris; A. H. Sayce
corpus_at_decipherment: Persepolis and Naqsh-i Rustam copies; Behistun parallel text; count unknown
method_steps: Royal names across parallel inscriptions → syllabic correspondences → Old Persian alignment → grammar
notes: An isolate; distinguish from Proto-Elamite and Linear Elamite.
selected_stage: 1853 Norris recovery stage (memoir volume dated 1855)

who: Bedřich Hrozný; earlier Knudtzon; subsequent Hittitologists
corpus_at_decipherment: Amarna letters; Boğazköy archive and lexical/duplicate texts; 1915 corpus count unknown
method_steps: Already readable cuneiform → bread logogram and water/eat forms → Indo-European hypothesis → grammatical testing
notes: Knudtzon proposed Indo-European affiliation in 1902. Hrozný’s 1915 productive argument used known logograms and cognate grammar. Lexical lists existed, but the opened account does not establish an extended Hittite translated key available to this breakthrough; partial retained.
selected_stage: 1915 Hrozný argument

who: Gelb; Forrer; Bossert; Hrozný; Meriggi; Çambel; Laroche; Hawkins; Morpurgo Davies; Neumann and others
corpus_at_decipherment: Monuments, seals, known names; long Karatepe Phoenician bilingual discovered 1946–1947; count unknown
method_steps: Names and logograms → syllabic proposals → Karatepe bilingual → cuneiform Luwian comparison → corrections
notes: Code the productive 1930s sign-mapping phase: short seal/name correspondences are partial keys. The extended Karatepe bilingual later confirmed and extended readings; it is not backdated into the first breakthrough.
selected_stage: 1930s sign-mapping stage (1935 plotting midpoint)
used_later_in_recovery: Karatepe extended Phoenician bilingual; Hawkins, Morpurgo Davies and Neumann 1973 revised sign values and linguistic identification.

who: Charles Virolleaud; Hans Bauer; Édouard Dhorme
corpus_at_decipherment: Early Ras Shamra tablets; 30-letter repertoire, word dividers; exact initial tablet count unknown
method_steps: Small consonantal inventory and word dividers; Semitic cognates/formulae → sound mappings; later refinements included the three aleph forms.
notes: Related Hebrew/Aramaic, rather than a translated bilingual, supplied the linguistic comparator.
selected_stage: 1930 alphabetic breakthrough

who: Alice Kober; Emmett Bennett; Michael Ventris; John Chadwick; Carl Blegen
corpus_at_decipherment: Knossos and Pylos administrative tablets, publications 1951–1952; exact count available to Ventris not established
method_steps: Kober inflection triplets and embryonic grid → Ventris expanded grid → Cypriot comparisons and place names → Greek hypothesis → Chadwick dialect analysis → unpublished-text confirmation
notes: Greek was a tested discovery, not the starting certainty; includes Bennett’s sign list and new-text verification.
selected_stage: 1952 Ventris Greek identification

who: George Smith; Samuel Birch; Brandis; Schmidt; Deecke; Siegismund; Ahrens
corpus_at_decipherment: Idalion Phoenician/Greek-syllabic bilingual and bronze tablet; early count unknown
method_steps: Bilingual names → sign values → syllabic Greek → longer Idalion tablet and grammar
notes: Eteocypriot in the same syllabary remains a separate language problem.
selected_stage: 1871 Smith Idalion mapping stage
used_later_in_recovery: Further syllabary and Greek grammatical consolidation in the 1870s.

who: Yuri Knorozov; Heinrich Berlin; Tatiana Proskouriakoff; many later epigraphers
corpus_at_decipherment: Three then-accepted codices, monuments, Landa sign explanations, living Mayan languages; exact accessible count unknown
method_steps: Landa syllabic key and pictured common nouns → substitution tests → later Berlin emblem glyphs and Proskouriakoff historical patterns → names and grammar
notes: Förstemann’s nineteenth-century calendar and numeral work preceded Knorozov’s 1952 phonetic entry; later historical names are not backdated into that entry code.
selected_stage: 1952 Knorozov phonetic argument
used_later_in_recovery: Berlin 1958 and Proskouriakoff 1960 historical/dynastic analysis; later phonetic and grammatical extension.

who: Jean-Jacques Barthélemy; earlier scholars
corpus_at_decipherment: Coins and Malta Greek/Phoenician inscription cast; exact early count unknown
method_steps: Greek names on coins and bilingual → alphabet matching → Hebrew/Semitic comparison
notes: A milestone in a cumulative recovery, not sole credit for all readings.
selected_stage: 1758 Barthélemy milestone

who: Jean-Jacques Barthélemy; John Swinton; Godwyn and other contributors
corpus_at_decipherment: Accurate paired Greek/Palmyrene copies published by Wood and Dawkins in 1753; count unknown
method_steps: Greek proper name Septimios → letter matching → Syriac and Hebrew comparison
selected_stage: 1754 Barthélemy/Swinton stage

who: Wilkins; Prinsep, Lassen, Pandit Kamalakanta and collaborators
corpus_at_decipherment: Repeated pillar/rock edicts, Sanchi donations, coin legends incl. Greek/Brahmi; count unknown
method_steps: Bilingual coin names → repeated donation ending dānam → shared edict formulae → Prakrit and Sanskrit comparison
notes: Wilkins read a later Brahmi inscription in 1785 (published 1788); reading back through later scripts preceded the 1837 early-Brahmi milestone.
selected_stage: 1837 early-Brahmi milestone

who: Masson; Prinsep; Lassen; Norris and others
corpus_at_decipherment: Greek/Kharosthi Indo-Greek coins; edicts; exact early count unknown
method_steps: Bilingual coin names → alphabet/syllabic correspondences → Prakrit morphology → inscription comparison
notes: Prinsep’s 1838 publication is a milestone; later work completed/corrected values. Coin name/title keys are coded partial, not an extended translated text.
selected_stage: 1838 coin-reading stage

who: Vilhelm Thomsen; Wilhelm Radloff
corpus_at_decipherment: Orkhon and Yenisei copies; Chinese commemorative parallels and names; exact early count unknown
method_steps: Direction and sign distribution → vowel patterns → Tengri/Turk and personal names → Turkic grammar
notes: Chinese commemorative texts are contextual parallels, not a literal interlinear translation.
selected_stage: 1893 Thomsen decipherment

who: Vitaly Shevoroshkin; John Ray; Diether Schürr; Ignacio Adiego and others
corpus_at_decipherment: Egyptian/Carian name pairs, funerary inscriptions; 1996 Greek/Carian Kaunos text; early count unknown
method_steps: Egyptian bilingual name matching → reject Greek-looking sound values → Anatolian language tests → 1996 bilingual confirmation
notes: Ray’s 1981 approach; independent Schürr/Adiego values 1993; short Egyptian name pairs are partial; 1996 bilingual confirmed later.
selected_stage: 1993 consolidation of Egyptian-name approach
used_later_in_recovery: 1996 Greek–Carian bilingual confirmation; not credited to 1993 keys.

who: Wilhelm Gesenius; Emil Rödiger; later epigraphers
corpus_at_decipherment: Early monumental copies; two medieval Arabic manuscripts with musnad alphabet keys; Ethiopic comparison; no exact contemporary corpus count
method_steps: Arabic manuscript alphabet keys and Ethiopic forms → tentative letter values → Semitic philology → corrected copies and further inscriptions
notes: 1841 identification of about two-thirds of letters is the selected milestone. Rödiger’s 1837 Arabic-manuscript alphabet note precedes it.
selected_stage: 1841 alphabet-identification milestone

who: Bushell; Morisse; Ivanov, Luo Fucheng, Nevsky and successors
corpus_at_decipherment: Khara-Khoto manuscripts/prints; Tangut–Chinese Timely Pearl glossary; Tibetan phonetic glosses; early count unknown
method_steps: Bilingual glossary → Chinese/Tibetan phonetic glosses → internal dictionaries and parallel Buddhist translations
notes: Bushell’s earlier work and Morisse’s 1904 Lotus Sutra study preceded the 1909 dictionary expansion; the chapter supports earlier identification, readings and Tibeto-Burman classification. Bushell’s specific 1896 character total is unverified here.
selected_stage: 1909 dictionary expansion stage
